author: evergreen reporter
title: Seattle man convicted on federal drug trafficking and firearms charges
text:
A Seattle man, Leon Henderson, 34, was found guilty by a federal jury on multiple drug and firearm charges. The verdict was announced by U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd following a three-day trial in U.S. District Court in Seattle.
Henderson was convicted of three counts of possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute, two counts of possessing a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, and two counts of unlawful possession of a firearm. He was arrested by Seattle Police on three separate occasions in 2023—January, May, and September—with each arrest involving over a thousand fentanyl pills. On two occasions, he also had loaded firearms.
During the trial’s opening statement, Assistant United States Attorney Jin Kim said: “Leon Henderson on the streets in his car was essentially a mobile office, from which he was selling drugs.”
Court records and testimony detailed that on January 25, 2023, police contacted Henderson at his car parked outside the Park Plaza Motel on Aurora Avenue. Officers found $2,770 in cash on him and discovered approximately 600 grams of methamphetamine, 1,700 fentanyl pills, 200 grams of fentanyl powder, and a loaded pistol under the driver’s seat during a search. DNA analysis linked Henderson to both this pistol and another gun found with narcotics.
On May 5, 2023, Henderson was stopped by police in Capitol Hill where he had about 7,000 fentanyl pills along with a firearm and cash. Later that year on September 13 in Ballard near a homeless encampment, officers arrested him with nearly 10,000 fentanyl pills inside his backpack.
In closing arguments Assistant United States Attorney Jessica Manca stated that during the Ballard arrest “police observed people coming and going to Henderson’s car window to purchase fentanyl pills ‘like he was selling coffee out of a drive-through.’”
Due to these convictions—including previous felony convictions for promoting prostitution and felony harassment—Henderson faces mandatory minimum sentences totaling at least twenty years: ten years for drug possession charges plus five consecutive years for each related firearm charge.
The investigation involved the Seattle Police Department and FBI as part of efforts targeting crime along North Aurora Avenue. The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms and Explosives (ATF) also assisted with the case prosecution led by Assistant United States Attorneys Jessica Manca, Jin Kim, and Carolyn Forstein.
